note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a No provision; A06b No provision; L05 SRI 19(3), 20(5), 21(1)): no ordinary naturalisation by residence; a citizen loses the citizenship on voluntarily taking another (with exceptions). Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: Generally applicable provision), A01b (descent, born abroad: Generally applicable provision), A02a (birth in country: No provision) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: No provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: not by birth in the territory alone (provisions for foundlings and children otherwise stateless, modes A03a and A03b, aren't held by the form); by descent from either parent, with no further limit on a child born abroad. Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file.

sources.title: GLOBALCIT Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (Vink, van der Baaren, Bauböck, Dzankic, Honohan, Manby; EUI Research Data, 2025), country-year-mode files, Sri Lanka, 2024
sources.said: n.a. ... n.a. ... Person is a citizen by descent or registration and voluntarily becomes a citizen of another country. Citizenship will not lapse if declaration is made for retention of citizenship and permission for dual citizenship is granted. This permission may be revoked at a later date. ... Generally applicable provision ... Person is born in Sri Lanka to a citizen. ... Generally applicable provision ... Person is born abroad to a citizen and is -within 1 year after birth- registered at the office of a consular officer of Sri Lanka in the country of birth or at the office of the Minister in Sri Lanka; Person over the age of 21 and whose mother was a citizen of Sri Lanka; Person is of full age and sound mind, resident in Sri Lanka, and was not registered in accordance with SRI 5(2). Other conditions: intent to continue to ordinarily reside in Sri Lanka, renunciation of citizenship of another country, and oath of allegiance. Minister may refuse the application on grounds of public policy. ... No provision ... No provision
